title: Finite invertibility of the counit-normalized exceptional transpose
statement:
Assume l ≠ D.p, the finite-field and finite-type hypotheses, and the coefficient data of [def-coef-system-dualizing-trace-data]. For the explicit map [def-coef-system-exceptional-transpose], the following finite-level assertion holds:
theorem integralDualizingSystemAdjunctionMap_evaluation_isIso
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S)
    (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (eQ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≅
        integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n)
    (t : IntegralDualizingSystemTraceData D l E X S G Q eQ)
    (K : (sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X)ᵒᵖ) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((coefPairingDerivedEvaluation l E n).map
      ((integralDualizingSystemAdjunctionMap D l E X S G Q t.trace).app K))

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: Fix the input K and level n. Integral residue Tor invariance puts its evaluated reduction in the finite-Tor constructible domain; no interval uniform over all inputs is used.

Evaluate the two adjunction transposes defining the comparison. Exact tensor and section comparisons carry the proper projection, open tensor inverse and evaluation to the finite-level word; trace_evaluation supplies the finite exceptional counit.

Finite duality site comparison identifies this word with the ordinary etale internal exceptional adjunction isomorphism. Transport back through the specified site and scalar isomorphisms; all these functors preserve invertibility.
